details.description: A short repository-level explanation of purpose and contents is missing; the existing README only contained a title.
details.why_required: Helps developers quickly understand what the package contains and where to find the implementation.
details.code_evidence: README.md contained only a title; source file: `input.ts` exports a single helper `fetchWithRetry`.

details.description: No guidance about the runtime requirement for a global `fetch` implementation.
details.why_required: The code calls the global `fetch`. Without noting this, developers running the code in older Node.js versions may encounter runtime errors.

details.description: There was no detailed API reference describing `RetryOptions`, default values, return type, and failure behavior.
details.why_required: Developers need to know the available options, defaults, return type, and how failures are signaled in order to call the function correctly.
details.code_evidence: Signature: `export async function fetchWithRetry(url: string, options?: RetryOptions): Promise<string>`; defaults: `const retries = options?.retries ?? 3; const delayMs = options?.delayMs ?? 1000;`; on non-OK responses the code throws `new Error("Request failed")` and returns `res.text()` on success.

details.description: No example showing how to import and call `fetchWithRetry` (or how to handle failures).
details.why_required: A short example reduces trial-and-error and shows expected patterns (async/await + try/catch).
details.code_evidence: Only `input.ts` exists with the exported function; callers must import it and handle the returned Promise<string>.

details.description: The README did not explain how non-OK responses are treated, what is retried, or which features are not implemented (timeouts, backoff, cancellation).
details.why_required: Clarifies what the helper does and does not provide so developers can decide whether to compose additional logic around it.
details.code_evidence: The implementation treats non-OK responses as failures (`if (!res.ok) { throw new Error("Request failed") }`), waits `delayMs` between attempts, and does not implement timeouts or cancellation.
